question.problem:
Given that $L\{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\omega t)\}=\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}}$ for $s>0$, find the Laplace transform of
$g(t)={\int }_{0}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2τ)\,\text{d}τ$
for $s>0.$
question.worked_solution:
We know that if $L\{f(t)\}=F(s)$, then

$$
L\{{\int }_{0}^{t}f(τ)\,\text{d}τ\}=\frac{F(s)}{s}.
$$

In our case, $f(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t).$ Thus, for $s>0,$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(s) & =L\{f(t)\} \\  & =L\{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\} \\  & =\frac{s}{{s}^{2}+4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying the integral identity above, we have that for $s>0,$

$$
\begin{aligned}L\{g(t)\} & =L\{{\int }_{0}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2τ)\,\text{d}τ\} \\  & =\frac{F(s)}{s} \\  & =\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+4}.\end{aligned}
$$
